clue.text: Garland for head man a restraint

parts.note: chap is an everyday word for a man
let means hindrance or restraint, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A head man is crowned with a wreath that also serves to hold him back.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or circlet worn on the head.

clue.text: Love, in short, requires craft in wooing

indicators.note: the love goes inside the short word

parts.note: curt means brief or short
O is love, a nil score in tennis
a ship is a sea craft

explanation.surface: Romance, in a word, takes some skill when chasing a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly'; in fact O goes in CURT ('short'), making COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship is the act of seeking someone's affections.

clue.text: Circling for miles, as lacking a fixed course

indicators.note: letters going round in circles end up in a different order

explanation.surface: A vehicle keeps going round for miles as if it had no route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circling' looks like a container signal, but it anagrams MILES and AS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without purpose or direction.

clue.text: Ascend alp in order to see this?

definitions.text: Ascend alp in order to see this?

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Climb a mountain to take in the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is the sweep of scenery a climber would see from a summit.

clue.text: Gather food

definitions.meaning: to draw cloth into a fold
slang for something to eat, especially at school

explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a stitched fold in fabric, and in British school slang tuck is snacks.

clue.text: Run and pass to slip back

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
time that passes is said to elapse

explanation.surface: A footballer runs and passes, then loses form again.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a former, usually worse, state.

clue.text: Stubborn Italian monk entering religious house

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a rectory is a parish priest's house
Fra is the Italian title for a friar or monk

explanation.surface: A headstrong friar from Italy moves into a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory means obstinate and hard to manage.

clue.text: Euro-currency that finally gets introduced in volume

indicators.note: the letter is brought into the currency word, as if newly admitted

parts.note: lire were the currency of Italy before the euro

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: A European money that is at last brought in by the cartload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that finally' gives T, the last letter of 'that', which 'gets introduced' into LIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of capacity, a measure of volume.

clue.text: Incomplete on one side

explanation.surface: Something unfinished on one of its faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means both not total and prejudiced towards one party.

clue.text: Duck's bill for penetrating always short

indicators.note: the bill is going through into the other piece
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ever means always
an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A duck's beak pierces something constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck's' looks like a bird's possession; 'Duck' is the verb meaning dodge, and 'short' cuts EVER to EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge it.

clue.text: Scare when armed assailant loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a gunman is an attacker carrying a firearm

explanation.surface: A frightening moment as an attacker with a weapon is overpowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to rob them of courage, to frighten them.

clue.text: Tea brewed with care if taken in this restaurant?

indicators.note: tea that is brewed is stirred up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Tea made carefully is what you would hope for in this eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' shuffles TEA and CAREIF together; 'with' only joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, the kind of place serving such tea.

clue.text: One's getting married, adhering to article of faith

indicators.note: sticking to something means coming right next to it, so these letters follow on directly

parts.note: the is the definite article
one's is short for one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: Someone getting wed keeps to a point of religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article of faith' reads as one phrase, but 'article' gives THE and 'faith' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god, a religious creed.

clue.text: Column heading out of fortified position after engagement

indicators.note: after places the fortified position behind the engagement in the answer

parts.note: a date is a social engagement or appointment
a line is a row of military defences, as in the Maginot Line

explanation.surface: A column of troops moves out of its stronghold after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' and 'engagement' suggest soldiers and battle; here the column is a newspaper one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dateline is the line at the top of a newspaper report giving its place and date.

clue.text: Wrapping concealing apparatus used for robbery

indicators.note: the wrapping hides the apparatus inside itself

parts.note: a bandage is a wrapping for a wound
a rig is equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Packaging hides a device used in a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigandage is robbery by bandits, highway plunder.

clue.text: Large number employed by a plant

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, as in a host of golden daffodils

explanation.surface: Lots of workers are taken on by a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosta is a leafy garden perennial, also called the plantain lily.

clue.text: Bags of old laws covering backsliding for instance

indicators.note: the laws wrap round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: rules are laws, ones laid down long ago

indicators.note: sliding back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to cite is to give something as an instance

explanation.surface: Ancient statutes deal with examples of people relapsing into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' turns CITE into ETIC, which sits inside RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticules are small drawstring handbags carried by women in former times.

clue.text: Deck for display crossing bay, perhaps

definitions.text: Deck for display crossing bay, perhaps

parts.words: Deck for display crossing bay, perhaps
parts.note: a showy covering laid across the back of a horse, a bay being a reddish-brown horse

explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth draped over a horse.

clue.text: Lover of the night air

parts.note: not a fan of cool evening breezes but a suitor singing a tune at night

explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is an evening song sung by a suitor beneath a window.

clue.text: An old pigeon, not a carrier?

definitions.meaning: the ... pigeon of North America, extinct since 1914
a traveller who is carried rather than doing the carrying

explanation.surface: An elderly bird that does not deliver messages.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct North American pigeon was named for its migrating flocks, and someone riding in a vehicle is carried.

clue.text: Showed teeth enmeshed

explanation.definitionFit: A dog snarled at intruders, and a line snarled up became tangled.

clue.text: Difficult question — or a sitter

definitions.meaning: someone who sits for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a thing is a hard question or an easy chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is both a baffling problem and a person who models for a portrait.

clue.text: Wise old man's upbringing that's based on scriptures

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means writing the word from the bottom up

parts.note: pa is a father, the old man, so with the possessive it is pa's
IE stands for id est, that is
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A sage's training was grounded in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'based on' stands NT beneath the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or discerning.

clue.text: Going downhill, powerless to align front of ski in finish

indicators.note: one letter is put inside the finish

parts.note: a coating is a surface finish, such as paint or varnish

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A skier speeding downhill cannot line up the ski tip at the end of the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to align' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the S from 'front of ski' goes into COATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasting is moving downhill without engine power, by momentum alone.

clue.text: Monarch crowned in spring

parts.note: crowned means given a cap on top
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A king or queen receives the crown in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful leap or skip.

clue.text: Wild animal heard in Siberian forest

indicators.note: heard means the word is said out loud

parts.note: a tiger is a big wild cat, found in Siberia too

explanation.surface: A big cat's roar carries through the northern woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the swampy coniferous forest of Siberia and northern lands.

clue.text: Operation at home following doctor's visit

indicators.note: following places the operation and home pieces after the doctor in the answer

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A surgeon's procedure happens at the house after a GP has called.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual call on someone.

clue.text: Consider reward, having been put up for it

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means writing the word from the bottom up

parts.note: meed is an old word for a reward

explanation.surface: Think about a prize after being nominated for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or regard as.

clue.text: Backing tip in taste for flutter

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the taste

parts.note: the palate is the sense of taste

indicators.note: backing up means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs a racing tip on a whim, going for a small bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns TIP into PIT, placed in PALATE; 'flutter' looks like a bet but means beat rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is to beat rapidly, as a nervous heart does.

clue.text: Right to have cast out broken pottery

indicators.note: the cast-out word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to shed is to throw off or discard

explanation.surface: It is fair to throw away cracked crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherd, or shard, is a fragment of broken earthenware.

clue.text: Send out carpet with reverse backing included

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: to carpet someone is to scold them, and to rate is an old verb for the same

indicators.note: reverse means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: aid is support or backing

explanation.surface: A rug is dispatched with a reversible underlay attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns AID into DIA, which goes inside RATE; 'carpet' is the verb meaning reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to emit or give off, as heat or light.

clue.text: Check metal in compass pointing wrong way

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means the whole assembled word is read backwards
the metal is put inside the other word

parts.note: room is scope or range, as is compass
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: Inspect the metal inside a compass whose needle points awry.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN inside ROOM gives ROTINOM, and 'pointing wrong way' reverses all of it. 'compass' is not the navigator's tool but range.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to keep watch over or keep a check on.
